findings.result: Retained core Dict uses a red-black search tree; every rolling-key increment calls Dict.update on that tree. The workload prescribes hash tables. Complete map contents alone do not satisfy that data-structure requirement.
findings.disposition: Needs guarded eligibility correction after independent evidence review; historical observations must remain available.

findings.result: HashDict separates hash projection from Equality.int key equality and stores original key/value entries in collision lists. A 32-bit hash does not by itself discard the 36-bit original key. Do not infer an equality defect from hash collisions alone.

Retained source searches an arbitrary >THREE substring, treats invalid bases as A and does not skip comment lines; exact-token, repeated-record, missing-record and comment fixtures are required before stronger input claims.
Tree balancing and repeated get/insert, seven String.foldl passes and tuple closures are hypotheses to inspect, not measured attributions.

retained_performance.comparison_scope: descriptive medians of retained cohorts; not a new paired experiment

evidence_limits: Official exact-version source fetched for review; its correspondence to every historical compiler-consumed vendor file still needs an archived build-manifest join.
No native parser counterexample, new source count or timing was run in this review.
No speed or optimal-source claim follows from using the hash library.
